name: ChatGPT
best_for_usecase: General-purpose chat, writing, analysis and brainstorming for individuals and teams
hidden_limits: Free tier has message caps and lower-tier models; Plus still throttles heavy use of the newest models and image generation.
ai_model: OpenAI GPT-6 family (Instant and Reasoning models)
pros: Broadest feature set: voice, images, files, custom GPTs
Strong at writing, coding and analysis
cons: Usage caps even on paid plans
Team plans cost more per seat

name: Claude
best_for_usecase: Long-document analysis, careful writing and coding with large context windows
hidden_limits: Usage is metered in rolling windows; heavy users on Pro can hit message limits during peak hours.
pros: Projects and Artifacts for organized work
cons: Rate limits can interrupt long sessions

name: Google Gemini
best_for_usecase: Individuals who want Gemini AI inside Gmail, Docs and Drive
hidden_limits: Top-tier model access and Deep Research quotas are capped per day. Google AI Pro is a personal plan; Google Workspace business plans are priced separately and are not covered here.
pros: Deep integration with Gmail, Docs and Drive
cons: Plan names and bundles change often
Privacy controls differ between consumer and Workspace

plans.name: Google AI Pro
plans.note: Yearly option is $199.99 billed once a year

name: Perplexity
best_for_usecase: Cited, source-backed web research and fact-finding
hidden_limits: Free plan limits Pro searches per day; advanced model choice and file uploads need Pro.
ai_model: Sonar plus selectable GPT and Claude models
pros: Lets you pick between several frontier models
cons: Weaker for creative or long-form writing

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Billed annually. Monthly price not verified yet. Personal use only.

plans.name: Max
plans.note: Billed annually. Monthly price not verified yet. Personal use only.

guide.intro: Perplexity is an answer engine that cites its sources. Pro is listed at $17 a month on yearly billing and Max at $167 a month on yearly billing, both for personal use only. Pro adds deep research, the choice between several AI models, and higher usage limits than Free.
good_for: Research and fact-finding where you want to see the sources behind each answer
People who want to switch between models from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and others in one place
Individuals: both Pro and Max are sold for personal use
skip_if: You need seats for a team, because Pro and Max are personal plans and Perplexity lists a separate Enterprise plan
You want a month-to-month price confirmed before you buy, as we have only verified the yearly rate

name: Microsoft Copilot
best_for_usecase: Organizations on Microsoft 365 wanting AI inside Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams
hidden_limits: Copilot has a free tier with limits. The cheapest paid plan we list is Microsoft 365 Premium ($19.99/mo per subscription), where AI features work only for the subscription owner. Business use costs more: the Copilot Business add-on is $21 per user per month at list price and needs a qualifying Microsoft 365 business plan.
ai_model: OpenAI GPT models via Microsoft Azure
pros: Works inside the Office apps you already use
Grounded in your tenant data via Microsoft Graph
cons: Value depends on how much you use Office

name: Ollama
best_for_usecase: Running open LLMs locally and privately on your own hardware
hidden_limits: Free to run, but model quality and speed depend entirely on your GPU, RAM and the open model you pick; no vendor support.
ai_model: Runs Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen and other open models locally
pros: Fully private: data never leaves your machine
Simple CLI and local API for developers
cons: Needs capable hardware for large models
Open models trail the best hosted ones

name: Midjourney
best_for_usecase: High-aesthetic concept art, brand imagery and stylized illustrations
hidden_limits: No free plan. Basic includes about 3.3 fast GPU hours a month, and extra GPU time costs $4 per hour. Unlimited Relax images start on Standard, unlimited Relax video and Stealth mode (private images) need Pro or Mega, and companies earning more than $1,000,000 a year must be on Pro or Mega.
pros: Strong style and character reference tools
cons: Images are public unless you pay for Stealth
Less precise text rendering and layout control

plans.name: Basic
plans.note: Yearly is paid upfront ($96).

plans.name: Standard
plans.note: Yearly is paid upfront ($288).

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Yearly is paid upfront ($576). Stealth mode included.

plans.name: Mega
plans.note: Yearly is paid upfront ($1,152). Stealth mode included.

guide.intro: Midjourney is an image and video generator sold only as a subscription. Plans differ mainly by fast GPU hours (3.3, 15, 30 and 60 a month), whether Relax mode is unlimited, how many jobs run at once, and whether your work can stay private.
good_for: Designers and creators who want stylized concept art and are happy to pay a flat monthly fee
Heavy users, who should look at Standard or above for unlimited Relax image generations
Anyone who needs privacy: Stealth mode is on Pro and Mega only
skip_if: You want a free plan to test with, because there is none
You run a company with more than $1,000,000 in yearly revenue and plan to use Basic or Standard, because the terms require Pro or Mega

name: Runway
best_for_usecase: AI video generation and editing for creators and marketing teams
hidden_limits: Everything is credit-based; video generation burns credits per second so the monthly allowance can run out in a few clips.
pros: Editing tools like inpainting and motion brush
cons: Free plan is a one-time credit grant
Output length per clip is short

name: ElevenLabs
best_for_usecase: Realistic text-to-speech, voiceovers and voice cloning
hidden_limits: Plans are credit-based by character; commercial licensing starts at the Starter tier and professional voice cloning needs higher plans.
ai_model: Eleven Multilingual v2 and Eleven v3
pros: Very natural-sounding voices in many languages
cons: Free plan has no commercial license
Credits run out on long-form audio

name: Leonardo.ai
best_for_usecase: Game assets, product visuals and consistent image styles with fine control
hidden_limits: Daily or monthly token allowance governs generations; private generations and faster queues need paid tiers.
ai_model: Leonardo Phoenix and Lucid models, plus Flux
pros: Fine-grained controls and custom model training
cons: Token system takes time to understand

name: Jasper
best_for_usecase: On-brand marketing copy at scale for content and growth teams
hidden_limits: No permanent free plan (trial only); brand voice, knowledge base and collaboration features are gated to higher tiers.
pros: Brand voice and style guide memory
cons: Overlaps with what ChatGPT or Claude can do

name: Grammarly
best_for_usecase: Real-time grammar, tone and clarity fixes across every app you write in
hidden_limits: Free includes 100 AI prompts a month and covers mistake checks and tone view. Pro is listed at $12 and includes 2,000 AI prompts per member per month, tone adjustment, full-sentence rewrites, plagiarism and AI-text detection. The page does not say whether the $12 is monthly or yearly.
pros: Works in browser, desktop and mobile apps
Team style guides on business plans
cons: Browser extension can slow heavy editors

guide.intro: Grammarly checks writing as you type. The Free plan gives mistake checks, a tone view and 100 AI prompts a month. Pro lifts that to 2,000 prompts per member a month and adds tone adjustment, full-sentence rewrites, citation consistency and AI-text and plagiarism detection. Enterprise adds unlimited prompts and security controls such as SAML single sign-on.
good_for: Writers who want consistent spelling, grammar and tone checks across the apps they already use
Students and professionals who need plagiarism or AI-text detection (Pro)
Organizations that need single sign-on and custom roles (Enterprise)
skip_if: You only need spelling and basic grammar, as the Free plan already covers that
You want a clear monthly price before you start: the plans page lists Pro at $12 without stating the billing period, so confirm it at checkout

name: Copy.ai
best_for_usecase: Go-to-market copy workflows and repeatable sales and marketing automations
hidden_limits: Plans bundle a fixed number of seats and workflow credits; extra seats and higher workflow volume cost more.
pros: Workflow builder for repeatable GTM tasks
cons: Product focus has shifted toward enterprise GTM

name: GitHub Copilot
best_for_usecase: Inline code completion and chat inside VS Code, JetBrains and GitHub
hidden_limits: Free plan has monthly completion and chat caps; premium model requests are metered and extra requests are billed on paid plans.

pros: Works in the editors developers already use
Deep GitHub integration for PRs and issues

name: Cursor

ai_model: Grok models on Plus; Claude, GPT and Gemini at API list price on Premium and above
pros: Strong codebase-aware editing and agent mode
cons: Usage limits can surprise heavy users
Pricing model has changed several times
Not a plugin: requires switching editors

name: HubSpot
best_for_usecase: Growing teams unifying CRM, marketing and sales automation
hidden_limits: Free CRM is limited to 2 users and 1,000 contacts, and shows HubSpot branding. Starter is listed at $20 per seat per month at the regular rate (new customers may see discounts) and removes branding and adds automation, AI agents, meeting scheduling, e-signatures and multi-currency. Starter limits include 15 pipelines, 50 workflows and 500 calling minutes.
cons: Required onboarding fees on higher plans

guide.intro: HubSpot Smart CRM starts free for up to two users and 1,000 contacts. Starter is the first paid step and unlocks the features most small teams reach for first: no HubSpot branding, automation, meeting scheduling, e-signatures, payments and email or chat support.
good_for: Very small teams that want a free CRM with no time limit
Teams that want to add automation and remove branding without a big jump in cost
Sales teams that value built-in meeting scheduling and e-signatures
skip_if: You have more than two users and need to stay free, because the free plan stops at two
You need Professional or Enterprise features: we have not verified those prices, so check HubSpot's pricing page first

name: Salesforce
best_for_usecase: Enterprise sales organizations needing a customizable CRM platform
hidden_limits: Sales Cloud now has five editions: Starter Suite ($25), Pro Suite ($100), Core ($195), Advanced ($395) and Max ($550) per user per month. Only Starter Suite is priced monthly or annually; the others are billed annually. Premier Support is an add-on on Pro Suite, and set-up and admin work are costs the list price does not include.

guide.intro: Salesforce Sales Cloud is sold as a ladder of editions. Starter Suite covers lead, account, contact and opportunity management with built-in sales flows, lead routing, email and calendar sync and email marketing. Each step up adds more automation, security and AI.
good_for: Teams that expect to outgrow a simple CRM and want one platform with a clear upgrade path
Starter Suite buyers who want a low monthly commitment at $25 per user
Larger sales organizations that need quoting and forecasting (Pro Suite), Slack Business+ and Tableau Next (Core), extra security (Advanced) or Agentforce (Max)
skip_if: You want a simple CRM with no jump in price: the next edition after Starter Suite is four times the cost per user
You cannot commit to annual billing, since every edition above Starter Suite is billed annually

best_for_usecase: Visual, multi-branch automation scenarios at lower per-operation cost
hidden_limits: Make bills in credits (most actions use 1 credit, some AI features use more). When credits run out, scenarios stop until you add credits or upgrade. Extra credits expire one month after purchase on monthly plans, and unused credits expire at the end of the term.
ai_model: Make AI Agents (bring your own model)
cons: Operation counting is easy to misjudge

guide.intro: Make is a visual automation builder. You connect apps in a scenario, and each action the scenario performs uses credits. Since August 27 credits are the billing unit, so older write-ups that talk about operations are out of date. The Free plan includes 1,000 credits a month.
good_for: People who want to see and branch a multi-step automation on a canvas instead of writing code
Small teams that want a low entry price: Core is $9 a month on yearly billing at 10,000 credits
Companies with fewer than 20 employees, which can ask about the Start-up Plan (50% off Business)
skip_if: You need a fixed bill: usage is metered, so a busy scenario can use up the month's credits and stop
Your volume is hard to predict, because extra credits expire and unused credits do not carry over past the term

ai_model: AI nodes for OpenAI, Anthropic and local LLMs

name: Mailchimp

hidden_limits: Price scales with contact count and the free plan has tight send limits and no automation beyond basics; unsubscribed contacts can still count.
pros: Handy audience tools and landing pages
cons: Costs climb as your list grows
Reporting and segmentation lag niche rivals

name: Buffer

name: Zendesk
